elements.label: Chem Ring
elements.description: A ring compound (benzene and its substituted forms) the source names or describes, where a real 2D structure reads better than the `◯` placeholder circle or a supplied figure. Rendered by RDKit from a SMILES string the agent writes — see book/format/ring.py and pipeline/subjects/chemistry/step07_formatting_agent/SKILL.md.
elements.notes: Not a guess from the Hindi name to the ring — the agent decides the SMILES the same deliberate way `chem-structure` decides a chain branch's position, and the code renders exactly that SMILES. Falls back to the plain `◯` circle (the `sp` element) when RDKit is unavailable or the SMILES fails to parse, never to a blank space. Reserved for a ring the agent can name exactly; the chapter's 79 supplied figures still own any diagram with curved arrows, a reaction happening ON the ring, or ambiguity about substitution pattern.

elements.label: Chem Structure
elements.description: A branched organic molecule whose branches the source describes in a bracketed sentence. 47 in chemistry chapter 6.
elements.notes: A GRID whose columns are the atoms, so a substituent sits exactly over the carbon it is bonded to and its vertical bond meets that carbon. Built as a grid and not as text because in a text line the browser decides where CH3 lands, and it landed anywhere: substituents appeared detached, carbon numbers floated free of their atoms, and a wrapped line put a branch under the wrong carbon. The source states every branch in prose; this only moves that information into the picture it was describing. Nothing is inferred — a sentence that does not match the grammar in book/format/structure.py stays prose, because a branch drawn on the wrong carbon is a different compound.

elements.label: Cover
elements.description: The opening cover page — a LINEAR stack, not a card grid.
elements.notes: The reference lays the cover out in source order: a `.source-front-title` masthead carrying `.chapter-badge` and `.chapter-topic`, then one `.source-front-section` per `##` analytics heading. A table inside a section takes one of two skins, picked by shape rather than by heading text: `.priority-table` for a ranked value column (each row a `.priority-topic` with its `.priority-id` chip and a `.count-value` pill) and `.study-table` for a numbered procedure (a `.study-number` circle per row). The older ~60 `cv*` classes are no longer emitted.

elements.label: Formula panel (सूत्र)
elements.description: The सूत्र panel — a section's formulas collected in one bordered card.
elements.notes: Each bullet splits on ' · ' into .fx (boxed formula) / .fd (caption) / .fc (शर्त condition). TWO SHAPES. Part 2 sets each result in a boxed `.fx` row with its optional `.fd` caption and `.fc` condition. Part 1's crib sheet sets a flat bulleted `.formula-list` instead, one `.formula-body` per formula — in a 449px column the per-result boxes drew a six-formula topic as six separate cards, so the topic read as six things rather than one. The panel is the same element either way; only the row shape differs.

elements.label: Matrix
elements.description: A matrix. Maths chapter 3 carries 496 of them.
elements.notes: Brackets are DRAWN with borders, not typed as [ ] glyphs, so they grow with the number of rows. Cells are a CSS grid with tabular numerals, so columns line up. A matrix is the one construct where losing the brackets loses the meaning: without them a 2x3 matrix is six loose digits. The same element also renders the INLINE matrices that format/inline builds inside a .m run; `matrix_art` is the block form, where each source line is one matrix row.

elements.label: Paper Ref
elements.description: One exam-paper provenance tag under a question head — `2024/set_a`.
elements.notes: `.question-meta` holds one `.paper-refs` pill, which holds one `.paper-ref` per paper. THE SEPARATOR IS CSS, not a text node: the tags were joined by a literal ` · `, which made each tag unmovable — dragging one past another left the dots behind in the old order. `.paper-ref + .paper-ref::before` draws it instead, so a tag is self-contained and the dots renumber themselves however the tags end up ordered. The BAND is declared here alongside the tag, and that is load-bearing: the editor decides what is an object from whether an element's own stylesheet paints a box, and the yellow is on `.paper-refs`, not on the tags inside it. Declared apart, a tag painted nothing, so it was read as running text — the same verdict inline maths gets, and the right one for maths.

elements.label: Priority Table
elements.description: The cover's topic-weight table — a ranked value column.
elements.notes: Each row is a .priority-topic with its coloured .priority-id chip and a .count-value pill. The third column only exists when the source has one; a two-column source must not get a blank ruled strip. Every cell carries a class so the editor can name it: `.priority-head` on the column headings, `.priority-cell` on the topic cell, `.priority-count` on the value cell (which holds the `.count-value` pill and any qualifier beside it, such as `लगभग`), and `.priority-marks` on the third column.

elements.label: Question paragraph
elements.description: Prose INSIDE a question — the stem and the answer's explanation.
elements.notes: 18.5px. The reference has 516 of these; rendering them as .para sets Part 2 a half-point small throughout. A second phrasing of the same question is `.q.variant-head` — `अथवा (2025 के विकल्प)` — an ordinary question paragraph, not a rule across the column. The marks pill that rides on the question head is `.qmarks` — a yellow-bordered chip, named here so the editor can treat it as the object it looks like rather than as a run of text inside the heading; it was the one thing on a question head that could not be moved or deleted on its own.

elements.label: Reaction
elements.description: A chemical reaction arrow, or a species carrying a name or a charge off the line of the equation. Chemistry chapter 6 (organic) carries 419 of them; chapter 4 (inorganic) 81.
elements.notes: The arrow is DRAWN with a border and a CSS arrowhead rather than typed as a glyph, so it stretches to whichever of its two labels is wider — a six-word reagent over a fixed-width arrow overhung it on both sides. Reagent above, condition below: that placement IS the answer to 'complete the equation', and printed inline it is unreadable. `overset` has two meanings and they are not styled alike: a label over an ARROW, and a charge over an ATOM, where the charge must sit tight against the letter because a carbocation's + a full line up reads as a separate term. See book/format/reaction.py for why all 500 were destroyed before this existed.

elements.label: Revision Flow
elements.description: Part 1's two-column spread. Its own design, not Part 2 restyled.
elements.notes: Each Part-1 block is `.u.revision-unit`. The skin it carries: a bulleted `.formula-list` सूत्र panel with one `.formula-body` per formula, a two-column green `.trio` fact strip of `.fact-item`/`.fact-label`, a `.subhead` section heading inside long answers, a red `.topic-frequency` seal beside a topic name, and `.derivation-note` for an un-rotated निगमन card. Part 2's question chrome lives here too: `.question-meta` holding `.paper-refs`/`.paper-ref`, plus `.inline-tag` and `.qref`.

elements.label: Stat tiles
elements.description: Three-or-so headline numbers with a label and an optional note — the cover's `पेपर सेट · उसमें इस चैप्टर के कितने अंक थे` block.
elements.notes: Tiles are only legible with short values: `4` sets at 34px in a 100px box, a sentence does not. When the data is not tile-shaped the component degrades to a compact list rather than forcing the layout. When the figures exist only in PROSE the deterministic path cannot extract them reliably in Hindi — it raises a review item and step03_content_tagger's agent supplies [{value, unit, label, note}] as a decision.

elements.label: Study Table
elements.description: The cover's reading-order table — a numbered procedure.
elements.notes: One .study-number circle per row. Chosen over priority-table by SHAPE — a numbered first column rather than a numeric value column — not by the heading's wording. Every cell carries a class so the editor can name it: `.study-head` on the column headings and `.study-step` on the sentence cells — the sentences ARE this table, and they were the one thing in it that could not be edited.

elements.label: Subhead
elements.description: A short blue heading: a one-line question stem, a bare उत्तर:, or a section inside a long answer.
elements.notes: One shape, four jobs — see `components/question.py`'s `subhead`. Measured on the reference: its stems run to a median of 25 characters against 108 for the ones set as bold body text, which is why a long stem stays a paragraph. Breaking a wall of answer into named sections is most of what makes a long answer readable.

elements.label: Topic Frequency
elements.description: The red “hot topic” seal beside a topic name, with its own yellow pin.
elements.notes: Sits inside `.topic-heading`, as a sibling of the `<h2>` rather than inside it, so the title can wrap without dragging the seal onto a line of its own. This IS the old `.examchip`, renamed to what the reference calls it: same seal, but the pin is a `::before` on the span instead of a separate element, and `flex:none` keeps it on the heading's own row. Both authoring dialects land here — see `components/inline.examchip` and `render._split_topic_freq`.
